=== DKT 56002 & 56003 STF-PIA-24 PD/STF-PIA-24-5 Trade Secret Assertion.docx ===
BEFORE THE GEORGIA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION

Georgia Power Company
Docket No. 56002 & Docket No. 56003
Georgia Power Company’s 2025 Integrated Resource Plan 
Georgia Power’s Company’s Application for the Certification, Decertification, and Amended Demand-Side Management Plan
STF-PIA-Data Request Set Number 24

BASIS FOR THE ASSERTION THAT THE 
INFORMATION SUBMITTED IS A TRADE SECRET


	As part of Georgia Power Company’s 2025 Integrated Resource Plan filed in Docket No. 56002 (“2025 IRP”) and Application for the Certification, Decertification, and Amended Demand Side Management Plan filed in Docket No. 56003 (“2025 DSM Application”), Georgia Power Company (“Georgia Power” or the “Company”) submits to the Georgia Public Service Commission its response to STF-PIA-24-5 (“Response”). In the Response, the Company has provided specific vendor information (the “Information”). All such information constitutes trade secret information of the Southern Company, Georgia Power, and its affiliates and is therefore protected from public disclosure under Commission Rule 515-3-1-.11.

	The Information derives economic value from not being generally known to, and not being readily ascertainable by proper means by other persons who can obtain economic value from its disclosure or use. Specifically, the Information contains confidential budgetary and schedule information related to projects at specific hydro generation facilities. Public dissemination of the Information would allow Georgia Power’s potential suppliers and contractors access to such estimated costs and timelines, thereby bestowing insight into the Company’s valuation of work and corresponding confidential budgetary information. Such access would grant an unfair advantage to contractors and suppliers of the Company, who could use such information to artificially set bid and proposal prices during contract negotiations. This could lead to the Company having to pay a price higher than that which it would have paid on a level playing field.

	The Information is subject to substantial procedures to maintain its secrecy. Only select Georgia Power and Southern Company Services personnel are granted access to the Information. Those personnel receive access only on a “need to know” basis. Parties outside the Company who have been granted access to the Information, if any, have been required to sign confidentiality agreements with respect to the Information.

STF-PIA-24-2

Question: 

██████████ is a major contributor for Distributed Control Systems (DCS), general systems and hardware across multiple sites.  Does the Company have a standardization strategy to maintain control system consistency across multiple plants? If so, please describe. If not, please explain.

Response:

The Company has a standardization strategy that applies to all Hydro Modernization Plants. This strategy includes standardized instrumentation, standardized logic, and standardized graphics for all units.  STF-PIA-24-10

Question: 

For all change orders listed as New in excel file Hydro Modernization Report Period Ending 6.30.2026 TRADE SECRET provide the root cause for all design changes including scope adjustments, vendor-driven changes, field changes issued.
Were any of these changes a result of any delays listed in the ██████████ tab. 
Were any of these changes to prevent future delays that may affect the broader hydro modernization fleet.

Response:

The Company does not perform root causes for design changes as a result of scope adjustments, vendor-driven changes, or field changes. STF-PIA-24-10 Attachment shows that the majority of the changes were discovery work. In the Hydro Modernization program there is a significant amount of work that is labeled as “discovery” because it is not possible to accurately scope the work until the components are disassembled, inspected, and/or measured. Other items on this list are labeled as “administrative,” which includes project carrying costs due to delays, costs incurred due to changes in applicable laws (tariffs are a common example), and changes in an individual contractor’s scope due to exclusions during the contracting process.

See STF-PIA-24-10 Attachment.

No. None of these changes were made to prevent future delays that may affect the broader hydro modernization fleet.

=== DKT 56002 & 56003 STF-PIA-24 PD/STF-PIA-24-1.docx ===
STF-PIA-24-1

Question: 

Has the Company considered using regional integrated schedules, considering the number of shared contractors and overlapping outages?


Response:

The Company has previously discussed regionally integrated schedules. However, due to the nature of the work and the structure of the individual projects, the Company does not believe that there is a benefit to using a larger, more complex multi-site integrated schedule. The management structure of the Hydro Modernization Team was designed to coordinate schedules across river chains and sites, and plan work accordingly based on resources. The contractor groups at modernization sites are very small (total site headcount is normally less than 20 people) so they are easily coordinated.

=== DKT 56002 & 56003 STF-PIA-24 PD/STF-PIA-24-8.docx ===
STF-PIA-24-8

Question: 

Provide GPC’s fleet-wide outage coordination plan for 2025–2031, including how overlapping hydro outages are limited to prevent reliability concerns.

Response:

Georgia Power Company participates in the system-level outage scheduling process for its 2025–2031 planned outages. This process limits system exposure by selecting outage windows to minimize reliability risk, managing system MW limits, and developing construction schedules to reduce outage durations. There is no separate formal hydro fleet-wide outage scheduling process. Hydro Services coordinates outages internally to maintain required flows and with Transmission regarding applicable voltage restrictions, while the system-level process provides the broader coordination used to manage overlapping outages and system reliability.
